title.en: The Cat and the Painkiller (Mark Twain, from Tom Sawyer)

text.en: Tom Sawyer hates his medicine so much that he finds a very odd way to get rid of it.

Aunt Polly believes in new health cures and forces Tom to take a bitter medicine called Painkiller. Tom pretends he likes it and asks for more. When she is not looking, he gives a spoonful to the cat Peter, who leaps wildly around the room and knocks things over. Aunt Polly finally sees what has happened.
The extract shows Tom's mischief and quick thinking and Aunt Polly's caring but fussy ways. It is humorous, and the writer gives characters lively dialogue. The novel The Adventures of Tom Sawyer is set along the Mississippi River in the town of St. Petersburg.
Words to learn: painkiller, mischief, dose, pet and Aunt. Notice how humour comes from a wild cat and a boy's clever excuses.
